 Rob Pelinka's work bolstering Lakers depth paid off yet again 
 Rob cooked... By Svyatoslav Rovenchuk | Nov 21, 2026, 1:01 AM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Sep 25, 2024; El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka at press conference at UCLA Health Training Center. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect When LeBron James walked out the door in Hollywood, Rob Pelinka decided his best strategy was to fill out a deeper roster around Luka Doncic. That offseason plan has yielded strong results. It just helped the Lakers steal a close 106-104 win against the Sacramento Kings on a Friday night where LA otherwise looked very beatable.
--> When LeBron James walked out the door in Hollywood, Rob Pelinka decided his best strategy was to fill out a deeper roster around Luka Doncic. That offseason plan has yielded strong results. It just helped the Lakers steal a close 106-104 win against the Sacramento Kings on a Friday night where LA otherwise looked very beatable.
 The Kings starters were rolling in this one, with each of them scoring in double figures. However, their bench could only muster up five points. Malik Monk scored two on 0-of-5 shooting and Emanuel Sharp pocketed a triple during a 1-of-5 shooting night from deep.
--> The Kings starters were rolling in this one, with each of them scoring in double figures. However, their bench could only muster up five points. Malik Monk scored two on 0-of-5 shooting and Emanuel Sharp pocketed a triple during a 1-of-5 shooting night from deep.
 Meanwhile, the Lakers reserves tallied up 34 points collectively. Collin Sexton led the efforts with 10 off the bench. Sandro Mamukelashvili broke out a shooting slump with nine points on 4-of-8 from the field. Jake LaRavia had six, Cameron Carr had five, and even Jarred Vanderbilt chipped in four.
--> Meanwhile, the Lakers reserves tallied up 34 points collectively. Collin Sexton led the efforts with 10 off the bench. Sandro Mamukelashvili broke out a shooting slump with nine points on 4-of-8 from the field. Jake LaRavia had six, Cameron Carr had five, and even Jarred Vanderbilt chipped in four.
 In a tight game like this one, that made the difference. The Lakers having depth pieces who could score was the difference-maker that helped them avoid disaster against a bottom-feeding Kings team. Pelinka's offseason focus on filling out a deep and capable roster paid off.

 Lakers bench stole the win against the Kings
--> Lakers bench stole the win against the Kings
 The Lakers improved to a league-best 14-3 thanks to their bench in this latest win. For a Los Angeles team that has struggled with their second-unit scoring during recent years, this was a refreshing change of pace.
--> The Lakers improved to a league-best 14-3 thanks to their bench in this latest win. For a Los Angeles team that has struggled with their second-unit scoring during recent years, this was a refreshing change of pace.
 Average (or just below) would be a fair way to describe the impact of the bench when it comes to getting buckets this season. That is noticeably better than 2025-26, when they ranked 29th in the NBA. That was not an outlier season either.
--> Average (or just below) would be a fair way to describe the impact of the bench when it comes to getting buckets this season. That is noticeably better than 2025-26, when they ranked 29th in the NBA. That was not an outlier season either.
 In 2024-25, the Lakers were also 29th in the league when it came to bench scoring. They had a lousy mark of 26.2 points per game from their second unit guys. In 2023-24, they were 28th with just 28.4 points per game. This has not been a team that could rely on depth scoring in recent campaigns.
--> In 2024-25, the Lakers were also 29th in the league when it came to bench scoring. They had a lousy mark of 26.2 points per game from their second unit guys. In 2023-24, they were 28th with just 28.4 points per game. This has not been a team that could rely on depth scoring in recent campaigns.
 The last time the Lakers had a competent bench, they made the Western Conference Finals. In 2022-23, Los Angeles was fourth in the league with 39.7 points coming from their reserves on average. This year's group are not quite at that level, but they are not the detriments that other recent teams have been either.

This year's group are not quite at that level, but they are not the detriments that other recent teams have been either.
 The depth even shines in aspects like having Quentin Grimes capable of stepping up for an injured Austin Reaves. Even with a lackluster shooting night against the Kings, Grimes has shined as a starter during fill-in duty. Add all that up and you see why Pelinka was excited to take the approach he did.
